sn9.1:1.2: On one occasion a certain bhikkhu was dwelling among the Kosalans in a certain woodland thicket.
sn9.1:1.3: Now on that occasion, while that bhikkhu had gone for his day’s abiding, he kept on thinking evil unwholesome thoughts connected with the household life.
sn9.1:1.4: Then the devatā that inhabited that woodland thicket, having compassion for that bhikkhu, desiring his good, desiring to stir up a sense of urgency in him, approached him and addressed him in verses:
sn9.1:2.1: Desiring seclusion you entered the woods,
sn9.1:2.3: Remove, man, the desire for people;
sn9.1:2.4: Then you’ll be happy, devoid of lust.
sn9.1:3.1: You must abandon discontent, be mindful—
sn9.1:3.2: Let us remind [you] of that [way] of the good.
sn9.1:3.3: Hard to cross, indeed, is the dusty abyss;
sn9.1:3.4: Don’t let sensual dust drag you down.
sn9.1:4.1: Just as a bird littered with soil
sn9.1:4.2: With a shake flicks off the sticky dust,
sn9.1:4.3: So a bhikkhu, strenuous and mindful,
sn9.1:4.4: With a shake flicks off the sticky dust.
sn9.1:5.1: Then that bhikkhu, stirred up by that devatā, acquired a sense of urgency
